lines.raw: PMPM (per member per month).
lines.say: P M P M (per member per month).

lines.raw: PMPM equals Total allowed ÷ Member months.
lines.say: P M P M equals Total allowed ÷ Member months.

lines.raw: For example: Member months: 7 members times 12 plus Daniel 6 equals 90.
lines.say: For example: Member months: 7 members times 12 plus Daniel 6 equals 90.

lines.raw: PMPM equals $91,800 ÷ 90 equals $1,020.
lines.say: P M P M equals 91800 dollars ÷ 90 equals 1020 dollars.

lines.raw: Report commercial and Medicare members separately.
lines.say: Report commercial and Medicare members separately.

Commercial. Members: 6. Member months: 5 × 12 and 6 = 66. Allowed 2025: 7970 dollars and 250 dollars and 180 dollars and 6400 dollars and 0 dollars and 5000 dollars = 19800 dollars. P M P M: 19800 dollars ÷ 66 = 300 dollars.

lines.raw: Medicare Advantage. Members: 2. Member months: 2 × 12 = 24. Allowed 2025: $12,000 + $60,000 = $72,000. PMPM: $72,000 ÷ 24 = **$3,000**.
lines.say: Medicare Advantage. Members: 2. Member months: 2 × 12 = 24. Allowed 2025: 12000 dollars and 60000 dollars = 72000 dollars. P M P M: 72000 dollars ÷ 24 = 3000 dollars.

lines.raw: All (blended). Members: 8. Member months: 90. Allowed 2025: $91,800. PMPM: $91,800 ÷ 90 = **$1,020**.
lines.say: All (blended). Members: 8. Member months: 90. Allowed 2025: 91800 dollars. P M P M: 91800 dollars ÷ 90 = 1020 dollars.

lines.raw: Do not mix different populations.
lines.say: Do not mix different populations.

lines.raw: Medicare members are older and sicker, so their PMPM is naturally much higher: **$3,000** vs **$300** here.
lines.say: Medicare members are older and sicker, so their P M P M is naturally much higher: 3000 dollars versus 300 dollars here.

lines.raw: The blended **$1,020** describes nobody.
lines.say: The blended 1020 dollars describes nobody.

lines.raw: If next year the mix shifts toward more Medicare members, the blended PMPM rises even if nobody's health changed.
lines.say: If next year the mix shifts toward more Medicare members, the blended P M P M rises even if nobody's health changed.

lines.raw: Always compare like with like.
lines.say: Always compare like with like.

lines.raw: Utilisation per 1,000 (also explained in the Eligibility course).
lines.say: Utilisation per 1,000 (also explained in the Eligibility course).

lines.raw: Admissions per 1,000 equals Admissions ÷ Member months times 12,000.
lines.say: Admissions per 1,000 equals Admissions ÷ Member months times 12,000.

lines.raw: For example: Emily 1 plus Thomas 2 equals 3 admissions.
lines.say: For example: Emily 1 plus Thomas 2 equals 3 admissions.

lines.raw: 3 ÷ 90 times 12,000 equals 400 admissions per 1,000 members per year.
lines.say: 3 ÷ 90 times 12,000 equals 400 admissions per 1,000 members per year.

lines.raw: Did the programmes pay for themselves?

lines.raw: (made-up 2026 example, Medicare Advantage group).
lines.say: (made-up 2026 example, Medicare Advantage group).

lines.raw: Cost saved. Calculation: ($3,000 − $2,500) × 24 member months. Amount: $12,000.

lines.raw: Care management for Thomas. Calculation: $100 PMPM × 12 months. Amount: − $1,200.
lines.say: Care management for Thomas. Calculation: 100 dollars P M P M × 12 months. Amount: − 1200 dollars.

lines.raw: Diabetes programme for Robert. Calculation: $25 PMPM × 12 months. Amount: − $300.
lines.say: Diabetes programme for Robert. Calculation: 25 dollars P M P M × 12 months. Amount: − 300 dollars.

lines.raw: **Net saving**. Calculation: $12,000 − $1,200 − $300. Amount: **$10,500**.
lines.say: Net saving. Calculation: 12000 dollars − 1200 dollars − 300 dollars. Amount: 10500 dollars.

lines.raw: Three traps when measuring.
lines.say: Three traps when measuring.

lines.raw: Small numbers:** with 2 members, one hospital stay changes everything; real reports need thousands of members.
lines.say: Small numbers: with 2 members, one hospital stay changes everything; real reports need thousands of members.

lines.raw: Regression to the mean:** people picked because they had a very bad year often have a better next year anyway, programme or not.
lines.say: Regression to the mean: people picked because they had a very bad year often have a better next year anyway, programme or not.

lines.raw: No comparison group:** compare with similar members who were not in the programme before giving it credit.
lines.say: No comparison group: compare with similar members who were not in the programme before giving it credit.

lines.raw: Also measure **quality**, not just money: did gaps close, did A1c improve, did ER visits fall?
lines.say: Also measure quality, not just money: did gaps close, did A1c improve, did E R visits fall?
